subject: Inference QoS checkpoints and post-demo action plan
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Alex Monroe <amonroe@veloxai.com>, Priya Rao <priya@nuvohealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T14:05:00Z
Subject: Inference QoS checkpoints and post-demo action plan

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo time earlier. Per our walkthrough, I pulled together a short QoS checklist and next steps so we’re aligned on the performance gating criteria for a pilot. Please review and flag anything I missed.

High-level SLOs we discussed
- Latency: P95 <= 250ms for 512-token streaming requests; P50 target 80–120ms.
- Throughput: sustained 3k tok/s aggregate per model replica (baseline), ability to burst to 6k tok/s for 60s windows.
- Concurrency: support 40 concurrent streaming sessions per replica with KV cache warm.
- Cold-start: first-token latency under 400ms for warmed containers; cold cold-start (scale-up) acceptable up to 2s but must not exceed 3s in worst-case.
- Streaming: chunked token streaming with <40ms inter-chunk latency to enable sub-200ms perceptual latency for UI.

Action items (MAP)
1) Nuvo provides 3 representative user prompts and expected token lengths by 08/14 — Priya.
2) Redwood to share an inference-config sample (batching, max-concurrency, quantization profile) and run a synthetic run with these prompts — Jasmine (ETA 08/14).
3) Nuvo to authorize a short test dataset and temporary API key for a 48-hour pilot — Alex (ETA 08/15).
4) Runbook: define fallback policy if P95 > 300ms for >5 minutes (canary rollback to smaller model or autoscale) — internal owners to draft.

Attachments: I attached a one-page checklist and a sample config YAML for quick reference.

If these SLOs look reasonable, we can schedule the pilot for next week and lock the evaluation criteria in HubSpot.

-Jasmine
Jasmine Liu | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Rao <priya@nuvohealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Alex Monroe <amonroe@veloxai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T17:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Inference QoS checkpoints and post-demo action plan

Thanks Jasmine — concise and helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 512-token baseline is good; many of our clinical prompts average 220 tokens but we have occasional long summaries ~1.6k tokens. Would you expect linear degradation or different kernel behavior at that length?
- For concurrency: the 40/session number is per model node or per pod? We plan to run two model variants (fast small model + fallback large model) behind the same route.
- Streaming inter-chunk latency: is the <40ms per chunk measured end-to-end (client to first byte) or only server-side? We care about end-to-end.

We can get the sample prompts by EOD 8/14. Also happy to set up an internal account and I'll loop Legal if we need a short-term NDA for the test dataset.

—Priya
Priya Rao | Head of Product, NuvoHealth

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya@nuvohealth.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-13T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Inference QoS checkpoints and post-demo action plan

Priya — quick answers before Jasmine posts the config run:

- Long sequences: not strictly linear. At ~1.6k tokens you'll see increased KV cache pressure and more memory-bound behavior; kernel selection may change (fused attention -> chunked attention). We'll include both 512 and 1600 token profiles in the synthetic run.
- Concurrency: the 40 concurrent sessions is per replica/pod as configured in the runtime. When you run two model variants behind one route we can route by latency/cost tier — the concurrency limit is enforced per variant unless you specify shared capacity.
- Inter-chunk latency: our <40ms target is server-side. End-to-end depends on client network; for the pilot we'll measure from a client in our us-east region and provide a small JS client to estimate RTT contribution.

I'll add the canary rollback recipe to the run notes (if P95 exceeds 300ms for >5 min trigger autoscale then degrade to fast-small model).

-Karthik

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya@nuvohealth.com>, Alex Monroe <amonroe@veloxai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Inference QoS checkpoints and post-demo action plan

Hi all — attaching the config we used for the synthetic run and a short results note. Summary: P95 (512 token synthetic) = 238ms with batching and token-stream enabled; burst test (6k tok/s) showed stable P95 under 290ms for 60s windows with autoscale to 2 additional replicas. The longer 1600 token test had P95 ~620ms (server-side) with our baseline quantization profile; switching to a different kernel/quant profile reduced that to ~420ms at cost of +18% compute.

Next practical decisions for the pilot
- Confirm whether Nuvo wants to prioritize lower latency for long-form (invest in different kernel/profile) or accept higher cost for that tail.
- Approve temporary API key and test dataset so we can run the client-side E2E measurement (will capture network RTT).
- Lock the rollback policy and which model variant to use as fallback.

Marcus will follow up on the exact run artifacts and a short playbook (autoscale knobs + rollback steps). Evelyn — can you confirm a customer SLA edge-case we should escalate for?

Thanks — Jasmine

From: Alex Monroe <amonroe@veloxai.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Priya Rao <priya@nuvohealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T10:31:00Z
Subject: Re: Inference QoS checkpoints and post-demo action plan

Appreciate the data and the config — that clears up a lot. Quick reply with decisions from Nuvo:
1) We prioritize lower latency on interactive prompts (<=512 tokens) and are OK accepting higher cost for the longer summaries for now.
2) We approved a 48-hour pilot API key (Priya will share NDA status) — please send the key and instructions.
3) Rollback policy is accepted: canary autoscale + fallback to small model.

We'll send the sample prompts this afternoon. Looking forward to Marcus's run artifacts and the JS client to measure E2E.

—Alex
